question: In its Vision for Agriculture and Food, published in February 2025, the Commission announced the preparation of a study on the impact of the consumption of ultra-processed foods, intended to inform the annual food dialogues. In view of this, I ask the Commission to clarify the following: 1.
What is the planned timeline for the completion and publication of this study?
How does the Commission intend to organise the methodology and governance of the study to ensure that the most up-to-date independent scientific evidence is taken into account?

What measures will be put in place to guarantee the scientific independence of the process, and how will it both avoid any influence from actors with commercial interests in the outcome and involve relevant areas of the Commission and stakeholders with a genuine commitment to public health?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.5.2026) The Commission announced12,that the study on ‘ultra-processed foods’ will rely on the opinions of the Scientific Advice Mechanism (comprising the Group of Chief Scientific Advisors (GCSA)3) and the European Group on Ethics in Science and New Technologies (EGE)4. The advisory process typically spans one year from the receipt of an official request for advice.

GCSA and EGE Opinions rely on scientific literature reviews, expert hearings and workshops. They are supported by the Horizon Europe-funded Science Advice for Policy by European Academies (SAPEA)5 and Support for the Activities of the European Group on Ethics by European Academia and Ethics Bodies (SAEGE)6 projects, respectively, that supply evidence review reports (ERRs) and independent expert panels.

SAPEA’s reports undergo double-blind peer review, while GCSA drafts are scrutinised by experts, the Commission, and external stakeholders. Declarations of interest are available on the Register of Commission expert groups (GCSA and EGE), or the Scientific Advice Mechanism to the European Commission (SAM) website7 (SAPEA working groups) post-ERR publication, to prevent lobbying.
All meetings remain closed to prevent undue influence.
